title: Five Hindi Films and Series Arriving This Week: Daayra to Lust Stories 3
excerpt: September 14–20 brings a crowded Friday, September 18, with three theatrical releases including Meghna Gulzar's Daayra, plus Netflix's Lust Stories 3 and Rohit Sharma's TV hosting debut.
body:
• Five Hindi titles arrive between September 14 and 20, with the action concentrated on Friday, September 18.
  • Theatrical releases are led by Meghna Gulzar's crime thriller Daayra, starring Kareena Kapoor Khan and Prithviraj Sukumaran, alongside Kunal Kemmu's directorial Vibe and courtroom drama Love Lottery.
  • Netflix premieres Lust Stories 3 on September 18, with four new segments from Vikramaditya Motwane, Kiran Rao, Shakun Batra, and Vishal Bhardwaj.
  • Rohit Sharma makes his entertainment debut hosting Family Full House on Sony TV and Sony LIV from September 19.

Three films hit theatres on Friday, September 18, Netflix drops a flagship anthology the same day, and India's most famous cricketer takes up hosting duties the morning after. Here is what is arriving and why each title matters.

In theatres: Daayra leads a three-film Friday

The headline release is Daayra, the crime thriller co-written and directed by Meghna Gulzar that opens worldwide on September 18. Inspired by true events — Gulzar has said it draws on several cases rather than one — it follows two senior officers, DCP Ajooni Kohli (Kareena Kapoor Khan) and DCP Raman Kumar (Prithviraj Sukumaran), who land on opposite sides of the same case after the brutal murder of a young woman. The 143-minute film examines punishment, justice, and accountability through two investigations pulling in conflicting directions.

Kapoor Khan called working with Gulzar a "full-circle moment" — lyricist Gulzar has a long association with her mother-in-law Sharmila Tagore — and described the filmmaker as a "taskmaster," saying the role demanded unusual restraint. Pen Studios chairman Dr. Jayantilal Gada said: "Cinema can entertain, but it can also ask the right questions. Daayra belongs to the latter."

Also out that day is Vibe, an action-thriller comedy directed by — and starring — Kunal Kemmu alongside Preity G Zinta and Sparsh Shrivastava. Two best friends, a clueless slacker and a diligent nerd, are recruited for a secret mission to protect India from a terrorist threat — comic misadventures follow. It is Kemmu's turn behind the camera as well as in front of it, and the lighter counter-programming to Daayra's intensity.

The third theatrical title is Love Lottery, a dark romantic courtroom drama from director Arvind Pandey. Akshay Oberoi plays Kartik Saxena, who becomes the prime suspect in the murder of his wife Bharani Verma (Heli Daruwala), with Kabir Duhan Singh as the investigating officer. Marketed with the tagline "A Man Framed By Love," it turns a seemingly straightforward murder trial into a tangle of buried secrets and conflicting testimony.

On streaming: Lust Stories 3 and a Sharma-hosted show

Netflix's biggest Indian bet of the week is Lust Stories 3, premiering September 18. The third installment of the Emmy-nominated anthology franchise weaves four unconnected stories around desire, modern relationships, and intimacy, each told by a different filmmaker: Vikramaditya Motwane, Kiran Rao, Shakun Batra, and Vishal Bhardwaj. The ensemble spans Radhika Apte, Konkona Sen Sharma, Vijay Varma, Abhishek Banerjee, Gurfateh Pirzada, newcomer Sana Thampi, Ali Fazal, Radhika Madan, Aditi Rao Hydari, and Siddharth — with real-life couple Hydari and Siddharth headlining Bhardwaj's segment.

The franchise has evolved since the 2018 original earned an International Emmy nomination, followed by a second edition in 2023. Produced by Ronnie Screwvala's RSVP and Ashi Dua Sara's Flying Unicorn Entertainment, the new edition examines vulnerability, agency, compromise, and desire.

"With every edition, Lust Stories has challenged conventions by bringing together exceptional filmmakers to tell deeply human stories."

— Ronnie Screwvala, producer, RSVP

On September 19, Family Full House with Rohit Sharma premieres on Sony Entertainment Television and Sony LIV — the cricketer's debut as an entertainment host, built around games, banter, and nostalgia, with guests including Shreyas Iyer, Shardul Thakur, and Shikhar Dhawan. Claims that the BCCI would act against Sharma have been widely fact-checked as false; the 39-year-old continues his ODI career and stays in India's plans for the 2027 World Cup.

Impact & analysis

Three releases crowding one Friday is a gamble and a signal: Daayra is the prestige play, while Vibe and Love Lottery fight for what remains. On streaming, Netflix counter-programs the theatres with Lust Stories 3, and Sony is using Sharma's debut to anchor its festive-season slate.

Diaspora angle

Lust Stories 3 streams on Netflix globally from September 18, and Family Full House will be available on Sony LIV's international service from September 19. The three theatrical releases will play in select international cinemas, where Gulzar's prestige and Sharma's star power both travel well with diaspora audiences.

What's next

The September 18–20 box office will show whether Daayra's positioning converts into footfalls. On streaming, the question is whether Lust Stories 3 matches the cultural footprint of its predecessors. And Sharma's hosting will be judged quickly — a three-match ODI series against West Indies begins September 27 in Thiruvananthapuram, so his dual innings start almost immediately.
